frameworks.name: comparative_advantage
frameworks.notes: France has one of the world's strongest civilian nuclear endowments: EDF (world's largest nuclear operator), Framatome (fuel, services), Orano (fuel cycle). Services trade (engineering, fuel, lifecycle support) is not in customs data — RCA must be inferred from installed-base share and EDF/Framatome order books, not HS codes.

frameworks.name: gravity
frameworks.notes: Nuclear services follow reactor vendor lock-in: customers buy services from (or licensed by) the reactor's original vendor. France's advantage concentrates where French-designed reactors or EDF-linked programs exist. Gravity applies via energy-demand size (GDP growth × electricity gap).

products.name: nuclear_powerplant_services
products.notes: SERVICE, not good — no HS code. Covers plant engineering, fuel supply (Orano), maintenance/modernization (Framatome), operations support (EDF). Team must decide how to treat services trade under Ricardo/gravity — this is a genuinely interesting paper question. (Submitted as null; stored as empty string to satisfy schema type constraint.)

countries.name: Poland
countries.notes: Building 6+ reactors; Westinghouse won first units but France/EDF pursuing involvement; large existing French trade relationship overall — the nuclear services link itself is NEW. Prime 'new link on mature channel' candidate.

countries.name: Kazakhstan
countries.notes: World's largest uranium producer; Orano JV history (KATCO); civil nuclear expansion ambitions; services link nascent.

countries.name: Indonesia
countries.notes: First NPP plans progressing; French nuclear diplomacy active; zero existing French nuclear-services link.
